key_insight: 2D/3D perovskite band alignment is highly sensitive to surface termination and composition, which strongly affects interfacial energetics and potential profiles.
engineering_relevance: Careful interface and surface engineering of 2D passivation layers can improve perovskite solar-cell stability while preserving favorable charge extraction.
method: Atomistic first-principles simulations with hybrid functionals
Computed work function, electron affinity, and band offsets across 2D/3D interfaces
Compared cleavages, terminations, and mixed-ions 3D perovskite compositions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that valence band offsets vary by about 0.2–0.7 eV and conduction offsets by about 0.25 eV depending on termination and chemistry.
watch_item: These are preliminary theoretical results, so experimental validation is still needed before translating the interface design rules into devices.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
